elements.label: Figure 4.7
elements.title: Developing countries face many more technical regulations than developed countries because of the nature of their exports
elements.content:
Line chart consisting of two panels (a. By product type and b. By income group) showing the average number of nontariff measures from 1996 to 2024.

Panel a: By product type
- Y-axis: Average number of nontariff measures, ranging from 0 to 18.
- X-axis: Years from 1996 to 2024.
- Legend / Series: Agricultural, Nonagricultural, All.
- Annotations: 'China joins the WTO' indicated by a vertical red line in 2001/2002.
- Trends/Approximate values:
  - Agricultural (Dark Green): Starts around ~1.5 in 1996, rises steadily to ~4 in 2002, reaches ~7 in 2005, ~9.5 in 2013, ~11 in 2016, and peaks near ~17 by 2024. Highest category.
  - All (Yellow/Orange): Starts around ~1.3 in 1996, remains relatively stable around 2-3 through the 2000s, increases to ~4 around 2008, ~5 in 2015, and reaches ~8.5 by 2024.
  - Nonagricultural (Blue): Starts around ~1 in 1996, stays lowest and relatively flat near 1.5-2 until 2008, then slowly rises to ~2.5 around 2014, and reaches ~4.5 by 2024. Lowest category.

Panel b: By income group
- Y-axis: Average number of nontariff measures, ranging from 0 to 12.
- X-axis: Years from 1996 to 2024.
- Legend / Series: Low income, Lower middle income, Upper middle income, High income.
- Annotations: 'China joins the WTO' indicated by a vertical red line in 2001/2002.
- Trends/Approximate values:
  - High income (Dark Blue): Starts around ~3 in 1996, drops to ~2 in late 90s, rises to ~5.5 around 2005, dips slightly, then increases sharply from ~6 in 2015 to ~11.5 by 2020-2024. Highest category in recent years.
  - Upper middle income (Yellow): Starts around ~1 in 1996, rises to ~3 in 2002, fluctuates around 4-5 until 2016, then rises steeply to reach ~10.5 by 2024.
  - Lower middle income (Light Green): Starts around ~0.8 in 1996, rises to ~4.5 in 1998, fluctuates around 3.5-5 until 2016, and grows gradually to ~5.5 by 2024.
  - Low income (Brown): Starts around ~4 in 1996, drops to ~1 in 1998, remains very low (around 1-2) until 2008, then slowly increases to stabilize around ~3.3 by 2018-2024. Lowest category in recent years.

Source: WDR 2025 team calculations, based on data from TRAINS [Trade Analysis and Information System] (portal), United Nations Trade and Development, https://trainsonline.unctad.org/home.
Note: The figure plots the average number of technical nontariff measures—sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade, and preshipment inspections—regulating each import market (origin-destination-product). The sample includes all countries surveyed for the TRAINS database since 2020 and all nontariff measures enacted since 1996. WTO = World Trade Organization.
